brand: Cold-Chain Guard | Design Master Solutions, LLC | QEMU + simulated sensor

scenes.title: QNX 8.0 boots in QEMU and checks itself
scenes.say: A fridge alarm must explain what happened, and what it could not observe. This is Cold Chain Guard on QNX eight in QEMU, with the boot sped up. The sensor is simulated, and this is a software prototype, not a medical device. During boot, the target runs our checks and reports each result on this console.

scenes.title: The fridge is a file: /dev/fridge0
scenes.say: Now the console is live. We start the guard with a synthetic excursion. A resource manager exposes slash dev slash fridge zero, so a plain cat returns temperature, validity, alarm state and escalation level. The alarm is active, at escalation level three.

scenes.title: Acknowledge the alarm: a name, not a fix
scenes.say: Staff acknowledge it by writing a name to the same device. The write succeeds, and the next read shows ack equals one, still at level three. This records the name and stops further escalation. It does not notify anyone, clear the fault, or verify the name. A duplicate is refused.

scenes.title: Limits change atomically, or not at all
scenes.say: Writing to the same device changes all limits in one step, and the next sample evaluates them, so this alarm clears, and the acknowledgement with it. Now an invalid command, with the low limit above the high one. The write fails, and the limits stay as they were.

scenes.title: Advice comes early. It cannot silence the alarm
scenes.say: Next, a warming fixture. The forecast fits a linear trend and offers advice before the limit is reached: alarm zero, trend to high, with an estimate. It is advice only. When the temperature crosses the limit, the real alarm fires. A forecast cannot delay, suppress or clear it.

scenes.title: Kill the daemon: SLM restarts it
scenes.say: Now the daemon runs under System Launch and Monitor, at fixed priority twenty. We kill it. S L M reports the abnormal exit and restarts it, and a different process serves the device. Its clock and alarm state start over, and the audit records one explicit unknown gap, instead of inventing what it never saw.

scenes.title: The portable core, on the host
lines: Selected literal output from this render
scenes.say: On the host, the portable modules build with strict warnings and sanitizers. These are real lines from this run. They support the target evidence; they do not replace it.

scenes.title: The audit from that boot, verified on the host
lines: Exported over the QNX serial console
Checksum, audit chain, byte equality with a host replay of the same CSV
scenes.mono_cmd: python3 tools/host/fgctl-extract.py build/console.log build/audit.bin build/fgctl build/ref.bin
scenes.say: The audit from that same boot left the target over the serial console. A checksum verifies the transfer, the verifier checks the chain, and a host replay of the same scenario must match every byte. It proves integrity only: a live log still needs an external trusted anchor.

scenes.title: The morning report, from this boot
lines: The boot's own acknowledgement check, exported over the same serial console
Chain verified before any HTML is written; times since process start
scenes.say: This boot's acceptance check also acknowledged an alarm and exported that audit. f g c t l report verifies the whole chain, then writes one HTML page: who acknowledged and when, in time since process start, not calendar time. A restart is an unknown interval, and the page lists what the prototype does not record.

scenes.title: Reproduce it. Then take it to hardware.
lines: Next: physical probe, persistent media, external notifications
Prototype only • no vaccine-safety or clinical claim
scenes.say: Hardware sensing, power loss validation and external notifications remain future work. Our public source and companion codelab show how to build and boot this with your own licensed SDP. Built by Design Master Solutions, LLC.
